h1: The 5 Best Large-Screen Tablets of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five tablets with 13 to 15.6 inch screens compared on display size, listed storage, stylus support and price range for 2026.
summary: The Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra is the best large-screen tablet, with a 14.6 inch display, 256GB of storage and an established brand behind it. The Callsky-Pro adds stylus support at a mid price. The MESWAO has the biggest screen, the JJGJ bundles a keyboard, and the TECLAST T65 is the cheapest way past 13 inches.
intro: Once a tablet screen crosses 13 inches, weight and portability start to matter as much as resolution. The trap is assuming the biggest panel is the best one, when a 15.6 inch slab that stays on a desk is a very different tool from a 13 inch one you carry to meetings. Screen size should follow where the tablet lives.

We ranked five tablets with screens from 13 to 15.6 inches, using the sizes, storage and features their listings state, plus the price range each falls in. We did not benchmark performance, and several listings are light on detail or stack confusing storage numbers in the title, so the guide flags every gap instead of filling it with a guess. When a listing will not say what a number means, assume the less generous reading.

products.name: Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra Ai Wifi Model
products.verdict: The established brand with a 14.6 inch screen and 256GB of storage.
products.description:
The Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra is the only large-screen pick from a mainstream maker. It lists a 14.6 inch display and 256GB of storage, which gives enough workspace for two apps side by side or a large drawing canvas. A major brand also tends to bring clearer service and update support, which matters on a device that costs this much.

It leads because the cheaper tablets below come from lesser-known makers and give you less to verify. The Callsky-Pro is nearly as large for far less money, but the Samsung is the safe choice if support and resale value count. It is the only $500+ tablet in this ranking.

Buy it if you want a large screen from a brand with established support. Skip it if budget matters more, since it costs the most by a wide margin. At 14.6 inches it is also awkward to carry daily, and the title mentions both WiFi and 5G, so confirm the version.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a large screen from a major brand.
products.skipIf: You are on a tight budget.

products.name: Callsky-Pro 14 inch Large Screen Tablet
products.verdict: A 14 inch tablet with stylus support at a mid price.
products.description:
The Callsky-Pro is the stylus pick. Its 14 inch screen, stylus support and a listed 16GB figure sit in the $200 to $500 range. A stylus on a big screen is the combination that note-takers and sketchers want, because the canvas is large enough to write at natural size.

It ranks second because it gives nearly the Samsung's screen size for far less, with stylus support included. The tradeoff is a less established brand, and the 16GB figure is unclear: it could mean memory or storage, so you cannot tell how much room you have for apps and files. Against the MESWAO, it lists more features.

Best for notes, sketching and split-screen work on a big display. Check what the 16GB figure refers to on the listing before ordering. Skip it if you want a major-brand warranty or a clear spec sheet.
products.idealFor: Note-takers and sketchers who want a big screen.

products.name: MESWAO 15.6 Inch Tablet
products.verdict: The largest screen here at 15.6 inches, with cellular listed.
products.description:
The MESWAO is the biggest screen in the ranking. It lists a 15.6 inch display and cellular connectivity in the $200 to $500 range, which puts it closer to a small laptop than a typical tablet. Cellular listed means it can work away from WiFi, if the plan and bands suit your area.

It ranks third because size is its only standout, and the listing is thin on storage and features. Against the Callsky-Pro, it is bigger but gives you less to verify, and it has no stylus. That makes the extra inches a gamble on an unknown spec sheet.

Choose it for a bedside, kitchen or workshop screen where size trumps portability. Skip it if you carry the tablet daily, because 15.6 inches is heavy and awkward in a bag. Check storage and cellular band details on the listing before you buy.

products.name: JJGJ 13 Inch Tablet - Android 16 Tablet with Keyboard - 32GB+256GB+2TB
products.verdict: A 13 inch Android 16 tablet that comes with a keyboard.
products.description:
The JJGJ is the keyboard bundle. A 13 inch screen, Android 16 and a keyboard in the box suit typing-heavy use and light productivity. The title stacks 32GB+256GB+2TB, three stacked figures that the title never explains.

It ranks fourth because the keyboard is useful, while the storage figures are confusing and the panel is the smallest in the $200 to $500 group. Against the TECLAST T65 below, it costs more and is a little smaller than its 13.4 inch screen, yet the keyboard saves buying a case later.

Best for typing-heavy use and students who want a laptop-like setup. Confirm exactly what the storage numbers mean before ordering. Skip it if you want clear specs or a pen, since stylus support is not listed.

products.name: TECLAST T65 13.4" Android16 4G Tablet
products.verdict: The lowest-priced tablet here that still exceeds 13 inches.
products.description:
The TECLAST T65 is the budget way to a large screen. It lists a 13.4 inch display, Android 16 and 4G, with a 20GB figure in its specs, priced from $100 to $200. It is the only pick under $200, which is its entire case.

It finishes last because the listing offers the thinnest detail, and the brand is lesser known. The 20GB figure is ambiguous in the same way as the Callsky's 16GB. Compared with the JJGJ, it has a larger panel but no keyboard in the box.

Buy it for a large screen at the lowest cost, such as a recipe screen or video display. Check the 20GB figure and the 4G bands on the listing. Skip it if you want a major brand, stylus support or clear storage numbers.
products.idealFor: Large-screen use on a tight budget.

whatMatters.detail: Screen size is the diagonal in inches. Above 13 inches, tablets get better at split-screen work and drawing but harder to hold, and they stop fitting in a small bag. The picks here run from 13 to 15.6 inches. Check the exact diagonal in the title, and compare it with a sheet of paper.

Storage is where your apps and files live, and some listings stack storage and memory numbers in one title, which makes the real figure hard to read. The Samsung lists 256GB plainly, while the JJGJ lists 32GB+256GB+2TB. Look for a clear storage figure before buying, and ask the seller if the title is ambiguous. Apps and offline files fill 64GB faster than most buyers expect.

A stylus helps with notes and sketches, and a keyboard helps with typing, but only some picks list them. The Callsky-Pro lists stylus support and the JJGJ lists a keyboard in the box. Verify what is actually included, since accessories are often sold separately and the price may not cover them. A keyboard that connects by Bluetooth also needs its own charge.

Established brands usually offer easier service, updates and returns, while lesser-known brands often cost less but give you less to verify. For a large tablet that may cost hundreds, support matters. Weigh brand against price, and look at the warranty terms on the listing, not just the title.

A 15.6 inch tablet is closer to a small laptop in size, while a 13 inch one is easier to move between rooms. The weight is rarely listed, so judge by screen size. If you move it daily, choose the smaller panel. If it lives on a desk or bedside stand, the bigger one is fine.

faq.q: What counts as a large-screen tablet?
faq.a: We used 13 inches or more as the cutoff, since that is where weight and portability start to change how you use a tablet. The picks run from the 13 inch JJGJ to the 15.6 inch MESWAO, with the Samsung at 14.6 inches.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake buyers make?
faq.a: Buying size without checking storage. Some listings give confusing storage numbers, such as the JJGJ's stacked title or the Callsky's 16GB, so confirm what each number means before you pay for a big panel with little room.

faq.q: Is the Samsung worth it over the Callsky?
faq.a: If brand support matters, yes. The Callsky-Pro costs far less and lists stylus support, but it comes from a less established maker and has an unclear memory figure, so returns and updates are less certain.

faq.q: Does the JJGJ include a keyboard?
faq.a: Its title says it comes with a keyboard, and it lists Android 16 on a 13 inch screen. Confirm what is in the box and whether the keyboard connects by cable or Bluetooth, since the listing does not say.

faq.q: How do I read the storage numbers?
faq.a: Look for a plain storage figure in the specs, such as the Samsung's 256GB. Some titles stack several numbers, and the TECLAST T65 lists 20GB, so ask the seller what it covers.

faq.q: Are large tablets easy to carry?
faq.a: Not always. A 15.6 inch model like the MESWAO is closer to a small laptop, and even the 14.6 inch Samsung is bulky in a bag. The 13 inch JJGJ and 13.4 inch TECLAST are easier to move between rooms.

finalTake: For most buyers who want a big screen they can rely on, the Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra is the best large-screen tablet. Choose the Callsky-Pro for a stylus at a mid price, the MESWAO for the largest panel, the JJGJ for a keyboard bundle, and the TECLAST T65 when budget decides.
